facts.fact: The BCEAO had granted one payment service provider licence in Burkina Faso by 27 May 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The BCEAO had granted four payment service provider licences in Cote d'Ivoire by 27 May 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The BCEAO had granted one payment service provider licence in Mali by 27 May 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The BCEAO had granted one payment service provider licence in Niger by 27 May 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The BCEAO had granted four payment service provider licences in Senegal by 27 May 2025, per Agence Ecofin.

facts.fact: BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 of 23 January 2024 governs payment services across UMOA and requires providers to be licensed, with the compliance deadline extended to 31 August 2025, per Agence Ecofin.
The instruction obliges fintechs to hold a licence, with capital of 10 to 100 million FCFA, and one provider was licensed in Burkina Faso by 27 May 2025.
